governed_construct: A form-validation site: code that validates user-submitted form data (a form resolver/validate option, a submit handler or server action that checks FormData / form field values / a form request body, or a schema defined and used to validate such input). Each such site is one instance.
interpretation: The rule requires that form input be validated through a Zod schema, i.e. a schema built from bindings imported from the 'zod' package (named, namespace or aliased import) and applied via parse/safeParse, zodResolver, or an adapter/validate function that calls the Zod schema. A form-validation site conforms only if its checks are performed by such a Zod schema. It is violated if any form-validation site uses another validation library (yup, Joi, validator.js, etc.), hand-rolled if/regex checks, or the browser constraint-validation API instead of Zod. What matters is what the validating identifiers are BOUND to, not their names: a namespace import of yup named `z`, or a local object named `z` shadowing a Zod import, is not Zod. Zod used only for non-form data (e.g. an API response schema) does not make hand-rolled form validation conform. Files with no form-validation code at all are NOT_APPLICABLE.
